'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Eurovision Song Contest 2021]]
**[[Måneskin]], representing [[Italy in the Eurovision Song Contest|Italy]], wins in the final of the [[Eurovision Song Contest 2021]] which took place in [[Rotterdam]], [[Netherlands]], with the song "[[Zitti e buoni]]". It is the first time that the country has won since [[Eurovision Song Contest 1990|1990]]. [https://eurovision.tv/story/dates-for-eurovision-2021-announced (Eurovision.tv)]
**The [[United Kingdom in the Eurovision Song Contest|United Kingdom]] becomes the first country to achieve "[[Nul points]]" from both the televote and jury since the current voting system was implemented in [[Eurovision Song Contest 2016|2016]]. [https://www.news.com.au/entertainment/music/uk-suffers-historymaking-eurovision-defeat-with-zero-points-from-jury-and-public/news-story/76d04488dec4f6f0d1efe24c3a2352d7 (News.com.au)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Gansu ultramarathon disaster]]
**Twenty-one runners die and eight more are injured when high winds and [[freezing rain]] strike a [[long-distance running|long-distance]] race in [[Jingtai County|Jingtai]], [[Gansu]], [[China]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-57216601 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Mount Nyiragongo eruption]]
**[[Mount Nyiragongo]], located in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], erupts. Thousands [[emergency evacuation|evacuate]] from the nearby city of [[Goma]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-57215690 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] releases information on a second, deadlier form of "[[Fungal infection|white fungus]]" infection that has begun spreading among patients initially placed at risk because of [[COVID-19]]. The newly identified white fungus is known as [[candidiasis]]. Steroid treatment can cause white fungal infection in COVID patients while unsterile use of [[oxygen cylinder]]s can also be a cause. White fungus infection is more dangerous because it rapidly affects vital organs and genitals along with the mouth, stomach and skin. The [[antifungal]] drugs [[fluconazole]], [[itraconazole]], [[caspofungin]], and [[micafungin]] are being prescribed to treat patients. [https://www.newindianexpress.com/galleries/nation/2021/may/22/white-fungus-outbreak-updates-what-we-know-so-far-about-the-infection-deadlier-than-black-fungus-103145--1.html (New Indian Express)]
****India's [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology]] writes to all social media companies asking them to [[censorship in india|remove content]] referring to an "[[Lineage B.1.617|Indian variant]]" of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/india-asks-social-media-firms-remove-reference-indian-variant-coronavirus-2021-05-21/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****The [[Government of Malaysia|government]] announces additional restrictions for the third [[Malaysian movement control order|movement control order]], including mandating 80% of [[public sector]] workers and 40% of [[private sector]] workers to [[work from home]], restricting the operating hours of businesses from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. and reducing the capacity of [[public transport]] and other [[mass transportation]] vehicles to 50 percent. These new restrictions will take effect on May 25. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/05/22/businesses-to-run-8am-8pm-starting-may-25-in-new-mco-3.0-more-to-wfh-cuts-t/1976244 (''Malay Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] reports a record 46 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 1,178. [http://www.colombopage.com/archive_21A/May23_1621709807CH.php (Colombo Page)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]], [[Lineage B.1.351]]
****[[Thailand]] reports its first locally transmitted cases of the [[South Africa]]n Lineage B.1.351 variant in three test samples from a cluster of infections that could be linked to [[illegal immigration]] in the southern portion of the country. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2021/05/22/thailand-finds-first-local-cases-of-south-african-covid-19-variant-scientists-say (''The Star'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***A nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] begins as [[President of Argentina|President]] [[Alberto Fernández]] says that the country is experiencing its worst moment of the [[pandemic]]. As the number of cases increases, only essential personnel are allowed to travel freely for the next nine days. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-57211697 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy]]
***[[Italy]] reaches a milestone of 30 million [[COVID-19 vaccine]] doses administered, with 9.85 million people fully vaccinated. [https://english.alarabiya.net/coronavirus/2021/05/22/Italy-passes-30-million-COVID-19-vaccine-dose-milestone (Al-Arabiya English)]
*[[Australia]] reports that it is suffering a plague of mice across [[New South Wales]], from the [[Queensland]] border all the way to [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]]. Mice are chewing through walls and ceilings, and are estimated to have caused [[Australian dollar|$]]100 million in damage to crops and grain stores. Homeowners setting traps are reporting catching 500 to 600 mice per night. [https://9now.nine.com.au/a-current-affair/country-locals-across-australia-video-worsening-mouse-plague-spreading/23990c4a-3546-4780-9e6f-2cb494996618 (9News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Bangladesh–Israel relations]]
**[[Bangladesh]] removes a passage from [[Bangladeshi passport|its passport]] saying that it cannot be used for travel to and from [[Israel]], thereby formally lifting the [[travel ban]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/bangladesh-lifts-ban-on-travel-to-israel-668854 (''Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Belgium–Democratic Republic of the Congo relations]]
**[[government of Belgium|Belgian]] officials announce that they will return the remains of Congolese independence leader [[Patrice Lumumba]] to his family, which is just a single tooth as his body was dissolved in acid following his [[assassination]] in 1961. The handover ceremony is expected to take place on either June 21 or 22 in [[Brussels]]. [https://news.yahoo.com/slain-independence-hero-lumumbas-last-134647029.html (Yahoo! News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]]
**New footage reveals that William Jennette, a truck driver, died in the [[Marshall County, Tennessee|Marshall County]] jail while gasping for breath minutes after police officers held him face down, with one taunting, "[[I can't breathe|You shouldn't be able to breathe]]." Jennette's official [[post-mortem]] examination had ruled the death to be a [[homicide]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57194883 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[International protests over the 2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**[[Protests against Benjamin Netanyahu]]
***Protests form outside the [[Beit Aghion|residence]] of [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] in [[Jerusalem]], accusing him of intentionally escalating the [[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis|conflict between Israel and the Gaza Strip]] in order to maintain his power. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/anti-netanyahu-protesters-to-gather-blame-pm-for-gaza-escalation-668825 (''Jerusalem Post'')]
**Over 180,000 protesters gather in [[Hyde Park, London|Hyde Park]] in [[London]] to show solidarity with [[State of Palestine|Palestine]], making it the largest pro-[[Palestinians|Palestinian]] protest in [[British history]]. Protests also occur in [[Bristol]], [[Peterborough]], and [[Nottingham]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/may/22/thousands-gather-in-london-for-palestine-solidarity-march (''The Guardian'')]
**Over 1,000 people gather at the [[Place de la République]] in [[Paris]] to protest in solidarity with Palestine. Unlike protests that occurred earlier this month, this one was approved by authorities. [https://www.urdupoint.com/en/world/some-1000-people-rally-in-support-of-palesti-1257023.html (UrduPoint)]
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**In his first interview since the [[coup]], [[Military junta|junta]] leader [[Min Aung Hlaing]] says that deposed leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] is in good health and that she will appear in court soon. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/myanmar-junta-leader-says-suu-kyi-good-health-2021-05-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[April 2021 Samoan general election]], [[2021 Samoan constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Samoa]]n head of state, [[Tuimalealiifano Va'aletoa Sualauvi II]], issues a proclamation preventing the [[Legislative Assembly of Samoa]] from meeting on May 24 without explanation, triggering a [[2021 Samoan constitutional crisis|constitutional crisis]]. Opposition leader [[Naomi Mataʻafa]] of [[Faʻatuatua i le Atua Samoa ua Tasi|FAST]] was expected to be elected prime minister at the upcoming session following a [[Supreme Court of Samoa|Supreme Court]] ruling upholding the results of the general election. [https://www.samoaobserver.ws/category/samoa/84480 (Samoa Observer)] [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/443159/sitting-of-samoa-parliament-cancelled-constitutional-turmoil-deepens (RNZ)]
*[[Nepal]]i [[President of Nepal|President]] [[Bidya Devi Bhandari]] dissolves [[parliament of Nepal|parliament]] and calls for new elections in November. Her office says that the decision was made on the recommendation of Prime Minister [[KP Sharma Oli]]. This is the second time in six months that the [[parliament]] has been dissolved amidst a political crisis. [https://www.dw.com/en/nepals-parliament-dissolved-president-calls-for-fresh-elections/a-57628429 (DW)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020–21 La Liga]]
**[[Atlético Madrid]] win [[La Liga]] for the first time since the [[2013–14 La Liga|2013–14 season]], after defeating [[Real Valladolid]] 2–1 on the final matchday. [https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/atletico-real-madrid-la-liga-title-suarez-b1852156.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[2020–21 Bundesliga]]
**[[FC Bayern Munich]] [[striker (association football)|striker]] [[Robert Lewandowski]] scores his 41st goal of the season in a 5–2 win against [[FC Augsburg]] during the final matchday, setting the [[Bundesliga]] [[Bundesliga records and statistics|record]] for the highest number of goals scored by a player in a single season, which was previously held by [[Gerd Müller]] for scoring 40 goals during the [[1971–72 Bundesliga|1971–72 season]]. [https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/lewandowski-s-41st-goal-of-the-season-breaks-m%C3%BCller-s-bundesliga-record-1.4572657 (''The Irish Times'')]
